prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

This is the ship of pearl, which, poets feign, Sails the unshadowed main,— The venturous bark that flings On the sweet summer wind its purpled wings In gulfs enchanted, where the Siren sings, And coral reefs lie bare, Where the cold sea-maids rise to sun their streaming hair. Its webs of living gauze no more unfurl; Wrecked is the ship of pearl! And every chambered cell, Where its dim dreaming life was wont to dwell, As the frail tenant shaped his growing shell, Before thee lies revealed,— Its irised ceiling rent, its sunless crypt unsealed! Year after year beheld the silent toil That spread his lustrous coil; Still, as the spiral grew, He left the past year’s dwelling for the new, Stole with soft step its shining archway through, Built up its idle door, Stretched in his last-found home, and knew the old no more. Thanks for the heavenly message brought by thee, Child of the wandering sea, Cast from her lap, forlorn! From thy dead lips a clearer note is born Than ever Triton blew from wreathèd horn! While on mine ear it rings, Through the deep caves of thought I hear a voice that sings:— Build thee more stately mansions, O my soul, As the swift seasons roll! Leave thy low-vaulted past! Let each new temple, nobler than the last, Shut thee from heaven with a dome more vast, Till thou at length art free, Leaving thine outgrown shell by life’s unresting sea!

Here are two polished options depending on your preferred context:

Yet, its delicate sails unfurl no longer; the pearly ship lies broken. Now, every chamber within its spiral shell—where its quiet, dreaming life once resided as the fragile creature crafted its home—stands fully exposed, its iridescent ceiling fractured and its hidden depths revealed to the eye.
>
> Year after year of silent labor expanded this shimmering spiral. As the creature grew, it continually abandoned its former dwelling for a new one, moving gracefully through radiant archways, sealing off the old doors, and settling into its newest home without ever looking back.
>
> We owe our gratitude to this child of the restless ocean, cast forlorn upon the shore. From its lifeless form arises a message far more profound than the mythical call of Triton's horn. Echoing through the quiet depths of contemplation, an inner voice proclaims: *Expand your horizons, my soul, as time steadily marches forward. Leave behind the narrow confines of your past. May each new phase of your journey be grander and nobler than the last, broadening your perspective until you finally attain true freedom, leaving your outgrown shell behind on the shores of life’s eternal sea.*

---

### Option 2: Professional & Reflective Tone
*Ideal for professional presentations, articles, or formal writing where clarity and rhetorical elegance are key.*

> Poets often depict the chambered nautilus as a pearly ship navigating bright, enchanted waters—a daring vessel sailing past singing sirens, exposed coral reefs, and sunbathing sea nymphs. Today, however, its delicate sails remain forever stilled, and the exquisite ship lies shattered. Every internal chamber where its fragile inhabitant once quietly lived and constructed its expanding shell is now completely exposed, revealing its luminous inner archways and once-hidden depths.
>
> Through years of quiet, continuous effort, the creature steadily built its shimmering spiral. With each cycle of growth, it moved forward into a larger chamber, sealed the doorway to its former dwelling, settled into its new home, and left the past behind.
>
> There is a profound lesson in this ocean-born relic washed ashore. Its silent form conveys a message clearer and more meaningful than ancient myths. As this inspiration resonates within us, it offers a powerful directive: *Strive for continuous personal and spiritual growth as the years pass. Leave behind the limitations of your past, continuously building a broader, more elevated mindset, until ultimate liberation is achieved—leaving your outgrown shell behind on the shores of life's restless sea.*

outputs.L3:
In his celebrated poem "The Chambered Nautilus," Oliver Wendell Holmes Sr. transforms a simple seashell into a profound allegory for the journey of the human spirit. Through vivid imagery and thoughtful reflection, the text traces a path from poetic myth to a powerful lesson on spiritual growth and continuous self-transcendence.

The narrative begins by idealizing the creature, presenting the chambered nautilus as a romantic, mythical "ship of pearl" that once navigated enchanted, uncharted oceans. This fantastical vision, however, gives way to the reality of the physical world. The once-vibrant creature lies wrecked and washed ashore, its life concluded. Yet, in death, the shell remains a work of art; broken open, it reveals a breathtaking and intricate series of spiral chambers that document the entirety of the creature’s existence. 

This internal architecture reflects the creature's extraordinary biological journey. During its lifetime, the living nautilus refused to remain static. As it matured, it continually expanded its home by building ever-larger spiral chambers to accommodate its growing body. With each new addition, the nautilus moved forward into its grander space, permanently sealing off and abandoning its outgrown dwellings. 

Observing this remarkable natural phenomenon, the speaker experiences a moment of deep spiritual epiphany. Rather than seeing the shell as merely a piece of ocean debris, the speaker interprets the creature's physical growth as a clear, divine message delivered from the heavens. The silent, abandoned shell becomes a teacher, offering a lesson on how one ought to live.

Ultimately, the poem delivers a compelling mandate for the human soul. It calls upon individuals to emulate the nautilus by continually expanding their spiritual and intellectual horizons. People are encouraged to build grander, more noble realms of thought and character, relentlessly leaving behind the limitations, mistakes, and outgrown phases of their past. This lifelong process of self-improvement culminates in a final, glorious stage: the ultimate freedom of the soul when it finally sheds its earthly constraints.
outputs.L4:
**Chambers of the Soul: Lessons from the Nautilus**

To hold the fractured shell of a chambered nautilus in one’s hand is to behold a masterwork of natural architecture and a quiet testament to the passage of time. Looking into its broken interior, one can trace the precise, elegant geometry of its spiral design. As the living mollusk within grew larger over the years, it faced a constant necessity: it could not alter the size of its existing room. Instead, it was compelled to build a new, grander chamber ahead of itself, seal off the outgrown dwelling behind a pearly wall, and step forward into the expanded space. The nautilus spent its entire life constantly moving forward, leaving its former sanctuaries behind to serve merely as structural foundations for the future.

Yet, this oceanic relic offers far more than a lesson in marine biology; it serves as a profound parable for the journey of human existence. When we observe the continuous expansion of the nautilus, we are reminded of the natural imperative of our own spiritual and emotional growth. Like the sea creature, the human soul is not meant to remain static. Throughout life, we inhabit distinct psychological chambers—bound by the limits of our past understanding, old habits, childhood beliefs, and former comfort zones. 

To stay too long in a chamber we have outgrown is to invite spiritual stagnation. True personal development requires us to recognize when a stage of life has served its purpose. It calls for the courage to construct new, grander spaces of mind and spirit: spaces built on greater wisdom, deeper compassion, and broader perspectives. We must constantly leave behind our outgrown self-conceptions and past limitations, refusing to let yesterday’s boundaries define tomorrow’s potential.

Ultimately, the spiral path of the nautilus reflects our lifelong pursuit of self-perfection. Life calls us to continually strive upward and outward, expanding the borders of our consciousness with every challenge met and every lesson learned. By leaving our former selves behind while building ever-more-stately mansions for the mind, we participate in a continuous process of renewal. It is a journey that persists throughout our entire lives, culminating in the ultimate transition—when the soul finally sheds its physical vessel entirely, stepping out of its earthly shell to achieve boundless, ultimate spiritual freedom.
